identifiedGaps.currentClaim: Centralia: The Mine Fire That Forced a Town’s Relocation
identifiedGaps.finding: The headline collapses the chronology’s voluntary 1984 acquisition program and later condemnation procedures into one uniformly forced relocation.

identifiedGaps.currentClaim: A fire entered abandoned coal workings beneath Centralia, Pennsylvania, and spread through a network of seams and mine passages.
identifiedGaps.finding: The cited chronology dates the fire and its response but does not document this ignition or underground-spread mechanism.

proposedCopy.title: Centralia: The Mine Fire and Decades of Relocation
proposedCopy.subtitle: Pennsylvania’s chronology distinguishes voluntary acquisition from later condemnation proceedings for remaining properties.
proposedCopy.opening: Pennsylvania’s Department of Environmental Protection dates the Centralia mine fire to May 1962. State and federal control efforts through 1978 cost $3.3 million and produced limited results.
proposedCopy.context: From 1979 to 1982, the Office of Surface Mining acquired 34 impacted properties and the state began air-quality monitoring. After fire-related subsidence severely damaged Route 61, Congress appropriated $42 million in 1984 for voluntary acquisition and relocation of impacted businesses and residences. By 1991, 545 residences and businesses had been acquired and residents moved; condemnation procedures for remaining properties began in 1992.

sources.title: A Brief History of the Centralia Mine Fire — Chronology

claimMap.claim: The chronology dates the mine fire to May 1962.
State and federal control efforts through 1978 cost $3.3 million and had limited results.
OSM acquired 34 impacted properties and the state began air-quality monitoring from 1979 to 1982.
Fire-related subsidence severely damaged Route 61 in 1983.
Congress appropriated $42 million in 1984 for voluntary acquisition and relocation.
By 1991, 545 residences and businesses had been acquired and residents moved.
Condemnation procedures for remaining properties began in 1992.
The fire entered abandoned workings and spread through a network of seams and passages.
